## Tutorials

You can update a record, or document as it is called in MongoDB, by using 
theupdate_one()method.

The first parameter of theupdate_one()method 
is a query object defining which document to update.

The second parameter  
is an object defining the new values of the document.

To updatealldocuments that meets the criteria of the query, use 
theupdate_many()method.

### Code Examples

```
import pymongo
myclient = pymongo.MongoClient("mongodb://localhost:27017/")
mydb = myclient["mydatabase"]
mycol = mydb["customers"]
myquery = { "address": "Valley 345" }
newvalues = { "$set": { 
  "address": "Canyon 123" } }
mycol.update_one(myquery, newvalues)
#print "customers" after the update:
for x in mycol.find():
print(x)

---

import pymongo
myclient = pymongo.MongoClient("mongodb://localhost:27017/")
mydb = myclient["mydatabase"]
mycol = mydb["customers"]
myquery = { "address": { "$regex": "^S" } }
newvalues = { "$set": { 
  "name": "Minnie" } }
x = mycol.update_many(myquery, newvalues)
print(x.modified_count, "documents updated.")
```

## Tutorials

To limit the result in MongoDB, we use thelimit()method.

Thelimit()method takes one parameter, a number defining how many documents 
to return.

Consider you have a "customers" collection:
